title: Early Achieving Carbon Neutrality Will Greatly Reduce Unequal Risk to Humid Heatwave in a Warming World
content:
Abstract

Humid heatwaves increasingly threaten the sustainable development of human societies and ecosystems. While carbon neutrality is widely advocated as a strategy to mitigate climate change, its specific effects on heatwave-related inequalities remain insufficiently quantified. This study quantifies global disparity in risks associated with humid heatwaves under scenarios with achieving carbon neutrality (SSP1-2.6, SSP1-1.9) and those without (SSP5-8.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP2-4.5). Achieving carbon neutrality will greatly reduce heatwave risks, with mitigation effect increasing from the early to late future periods. Achieving carbon neutrality by the 2050s (SSP1-1.9) reduces risks in the late future by approximately 45% compared to non-neutrality pathways (SSP2-4.5), offering more significant mitigation than achieving it by the 2070s (SSP1-2.6). Moreover, SSP1-1.9 is the only scenario that leads to a decline in the intensity, exposure, and risks of humid heatwaves across the entire future periods. Furthermore, achieving carbon neutrality also reduces disparities between higher- and lower-income countries and between the Global South and the Global North, and this mitigation of disparities becomes more pronounced over time. Risk disparity between lower- and higher-income countries decreases to 21.8% of that under SSP2-4.5. These findings highlight the vital contribution of carbon neutrality in alleviating heat risks and associated disparities, contributing to climate fairness and informed mitigation.
